text:
julia (support): FYI — AcmeMaps reported a spike of 5xxs starting ~2026-03-15T10:30Z across hosted inference endpoints. They saw a ton of 502/503 gateway responses and client errors. Customer says it affects production routing (some calls succeed, many 5xx). Request IDs: r:acme-1023, r:acme-1024, r:acme-1031. Raising an escalation.

julia (support): sample error body they pasted: `{"error":"control_plane_error","message":"internal server error","request_id":"r:acme-1024"}`

maria (sre): looking. Any recent deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy to prod finished 2026-03-15T10:18Z (rev: a1b2c3) :rocket:

maria (sre): ok deployed ~12m before start of spike. I'll check control-plane dependencies: auth/session service, routing-policy, config-db.

samir (platform): metrics show elevated 5xx from control-plane proxies (gateway). Latency to config-db spiked and TCP retries increased. Graph: configdb p90 query time jumped from 30ms -> 1.2s around 10:29Z.

julia (support): customer timeline: first 502 at 10:31, burst between 10:31-10:40, then partial recovery ~10:50 but still errors for some calls. They asked for ETA and workaround.

maria (sre): can you paste a failing curl from the customer? want to repro quickly.

julia (support): they provided this repro:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-..." \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-large","input":"ping"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
`{"error":"control_plane_error","code":502,"request_id":"r:acme-1024"}`

maria (sre): I see repeated `timeout waiting for configdb` around those request_ids in the proxy logs. Pasting snippet: 
```
[10:31:15Z] proxy[handler]: ERROR request_id=r:acme-1024 upstream=configdb timeout after 1000ms
[10:31:16Z] routing-policy: WARN request_id=r:acme-1024 no route found (fallback attempted)
[10:31:16Z] auth-session: ERROR session-fetch timeout (conn pool exhausted)
```

maria (sre): auth-bot, any alert on session store?

auth-bot: detected 4xx/5xx increase on session-store calls, avg latency > 800ms, redis connection pool 96% used.

devin (eng-runtime): routing-policy service also logged many `DB read timeout` which causes it to return 500 to callers. That explains the 5xx bubble. Looks like routing-policy queries config DB per request and doesn't cache for this model route.

samir (platform): can we switch routing-policy to a cached path or increase DB read timeouts? We should avoid restarting services that would cause additional failures.

maria (sre): short term mitigations: 1) enable routing-policy in-memory cache for known static routes (toggle existing flag), 2) increase config-db read timeout from 1s -> 2.5s, 3) temporarily route heavy customers to a fallback model variant (lower QPS). Which is quickest?

devin (eng-runtime): toggle cache flag is fastest. It's a runtime config change via the control plane: `PUT /internal/config/routing_policy?cache=true` (doesn't require deploy).

samir (platform): I can flip that now and monitor. Doing it in Canary region first.

samir (platform): (10:42Z) flipped routing_policy.cache=true in canary. Observed immediate drop in routing-policy DB read calls for canary slice.

maria (sre): good — promote to global in 2m if canary stays stable. Also bumping configdb client timeout in proxy to 2500ms (hotpatch config).

samir (platform): (10:45Z) promoted cache=true global. configdb client timeout updated and reloaded on proxies (no restart).

maria (sre): monitoring: 5xx rate is falling. p95 latency back to normal. I'll hold until 11:00Z to ensure stability.

julia (support): customer update draft: "We're investigating a transient control-plane dependency issue that caused routing and auth lookups to time out, resulting in intermittent 502/503 responses. We've applied a temporary caching and config change to mitigate impact. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with root cause and a permanent fix." Thoughts?

devin (eng-runtime): message looks good. Add: "No customer data was exposed; this was an availability issue only."

julia (support): added. Sending to customer now. :white_check_mark:

maria (sre): postmortem note for RC: root cause appears to be an inefficient DB access pattern in routing-policy (N+1 reads per request for route metadata) plus insufficient connection pool sizing on session store leading to head-of-line stalls during a traffic burst. The new hotfix (cache + longer timeouts) stops the immediate failures but we need a code fix.

devin (eng-runtime): action items:
- devin: implement route metadata caching inside routing-policy (remove N+1) + add fallback TTL (ETA 2 days)
- samir: increase config DB read pool and add circuit-breaker on DB client (ETA 1 day)
- maria: add an alert for configdb p95 > 200ms and for session-store conn pool > 80% (ETA 4h)
- julia: follow up with AcmeMaps with RCA and timeline (ETA EOD)

samir (platform): also adding short-term change: increase redis connection pool for session-store by 25% (rolling config) to avoid conn exhaustion during bursts. Doing it in 15m window.

maria (sre): can we reproduce locally quickly? devin, do you have a test that simulates routing-policy N+1?

devin (eng-runtime): yes I have a script. Running a 500rps local sim reproduces high DB read count and eventual timeouts. I'll attach synthetic test results to the PR.

julia (support): customer confirmed errors have dropped and are seeing normal traffic. They asked for a formal RCA when ready.

maria (sre): keeping thread open until code fix merged and monitoring configured. Closing steps: add postmortem, include timeline, and link to incident page.

julia (support): final customer note sent at 11:05Z with interim RCA and next steps.

maria (sre): post-incident checklist done: alerts created, caches toggled, config changes recorded, owners assigned. Will draft postmortem.

devin (eng-runtime): PR for routing-policy caching opened -> link: https://git.redwood.ai/routing-policy/pulls/142 (description: remove N+1 by prefetching route metadata and local TTL cache).

samir (platform): rolling redis pool bump completed at 11:20Z. Observed fewer auth session timeouts after bump.

maria (sre): final note: root cause = routing-policy inefficient DB usage + insufficient session-store pool leading to cascading timeouts, which surfaced as control-plane 5xx. Permanent fix planned (routing-policy change + infra sizing + DB circuit breakers).

julia (support): thanks everyone — I'll keep AcmeMaps posted and close ticket after RCA doc is ready. :handshake:

maria (sre): :thumbsup: closing in 24h if no further regressions.
